Don't buy a US stock before you know these five things.
In the IND money app, open US stocks. Finish your KYC, sign form W-8 BEN, add money, and buy. Even a small fraction of one share.

Your rupees get converted to dollars, and banks charge about half to one point two percent for that. Brokerage is point two five percent a trade, plus GST. Above ten lakh rupees a year, twenty percent TCS is collected, but you claim it back in your tax return.
Three. Tax. This part surprises people.

Sell within two years, and gains are taxed at your slab rate. Hold longer than two years, and it's twelve point five percent. Dividends lose twenty five percent in the US, but you claim that credit in India. And report it in Schedule F A.
Pros. You own the world's biggest companies, and you gain when the dollar rises. Cons. You pay conversion both ways, the market opens late at night, and a stronger rupee can shrink your returns.
